targetText: The healthy sensuality of the middle ages found its classic exponent in Luther. We are here not so much concerned with the religious reformer, but with Luther, the man.
summary: Analyzing the Protestant Reformation, Bebel shows that Martin Luther's opposition to celibacy and monasticism reflected the economic and demographic needs of rising bourgeois and princely society rather than genuine liberation for women.
